title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Medical Entrance Exam
summary: Explore the science of medicine through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
From cells to whole systems.
How much can you connect?

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of the science of medicine. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a medical-school admission exam, professional qualification, diagnosis or medical advice.

medical-s1q1.question: Which gas does blood pick up in the lungs?

medical-s1q2.question: Which organs remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance?

medical-s1q3.question: Which system carries rapid signals between the brain and the body?

medical-s1q4.question: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed?

medical-s1q5.question: Which blood cells carry most of the oxygen in blood?

medical-s1q6.question: Which major muscle helps draw air into the lungs?

medical-s1q7.question: Which heart chamber receives blood returning from the lungs?

medical-s2q1.question: Which structure contains most of the DNA in a typical human cell?

medical-s2q3.question: What is a major role of mitochondria?

medical-s2q4.question: What forms the main boundary of a human cell?

answers.a1: Movement that always requires a heart
answers.a3: The conversion of every liquid into a gas
answers.a4: Net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration

medical-s2q6.question: What happens during mitosis in a typical human body cell?

answers.a2: Duplicated chromosomes are separated into two nuclei
answers.a4: Only the cell membrane is copied

medical-s2q7.question: Which molecule carries inherited genetic instructions?

medical-s3q1.question: Which tissue covers surfaces and lines many body cavities?

medical-s3q2.question: Which tissue is specialised for contraction?

medical-s3q3.question: What connects a muscle to a bone?

medical-s3q4.question: What connects one bone to another at a joint?

medical-s3q5.question: Which tissue stores much of the body’s energy as fat?

medical-s3q6.question: What is a neuron specialised to do?

medical-s3q7.question: Which description places structures in order from smaller to larger?

medical-s4q1.question: What is the main function of haemoglobin in red blood cells?

medical-s4q2.question: Which hormone helps lower blood glucose by promoting uptake and storage?

medical-s4q3.question: Which process moves water across a selectively permeable membrane?

medical-s4q4.question: What prevents blood from flowing backwards through the heart?

medical-s4q6.question: When body temperature rises, sweating helps cooling mainly through what?

medical-s4q7.question: What is negative feedback in body regulation?

answers.a1: A response that always amplifies a change
answers.a2: A response that opposes a change from the regulated range
answers.a3: A conscious criticism of an action
answers.a4: The complete absence of a response

medical-s5q1.question: Which infectious agents need host cells to reproduce?

medical-s5q2.question: Which group includes yeasts and moulds?

medical-s5q3.question: What does a culture test attempt to grow from a sample?

answers.a1: Bacteria can survive medicines that would normally inhibit or kill them
answers.a2: The body becomes immune to every medicine

medical-s5q5.question: Which organisms normally live on and in a healthy human body?

medical-s5q6.question: Which process destroys all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores, when correctly performed?

medical-s5q7.question: What can contaminated hands do in the chain of infection?

answers.a2: Transfer microorganisms between surfaces and people
answers.a3: Change every virus into a fungus

medical-s6q1.question: An analgesic is intended primarily to reduce what?

medical-s6q2.question: An antipyretic is used primarily to reduce what?

medical-s6q3.question: What does a medicine’s route of administration describe?

answers.a1: Two packages have the same colour
answers.a3: One substance changes the effect of another
answers.a4: A tablet is moved to a shelf

answers.a1: The cost printed on a receipt
answers.a4: An unwanted harmful effect associated with a treatment

medical-s6q6.question: Why distinguish a medicine’s generic name from its brand name?

answers.a1: Different brands may contain the same active ingredient
answers.a3: Every brand always contains a different ingredient
answers.a4: Generic names describe only package size

medical-s6q7.question: A medicine label is unclear. What should happen before administration?

answers.a1: Clarify it through the appropriate qualified professional
answers.a3: Assume all similar packages are identical

medical-s7q1.question: Hands are visibly dirty. Which cleaning method is appropriate?

answers.a4: Put gloves on over the dirt

medical-s7q2.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?

answers.a1: Clean hands only if a glove tore
answers.a3: Keep the gloves for another person

medical-s7q3.question: Which container is designed for used needles and other sharps?

answers.a1: An open tray for later sorting

medical-s7q4.question: A task may splash body fluid toward the face. Which protection addresses that risk?

medical-s7q5.question: Shared observation equipment has been used. What should happen before reuse?

answers.a1: Clean it using the approved method
answers.a3: Use it unchanged if it looks shiny
answers.a4: Cover old marks with a label

medical-s7q6.question: A sterile package is torn before use. What is the safe conclusion?

answers.a1: The printed date cancels the tear
answers.a2: The contents are sterile if they look clean

medical-s7q7.question: Which statement about protective gloves is correct?

answers.a1: They do not replace hand hygiene
answers.a2: The same pair is suitable for every patient
answers.a4: They stay clean regardless of what they touch

medical-s8q1.question: A record shows 750 mL plus 250 mL. What is the total?

medical-s8q2.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 L?

medical-s8q3.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?

medical-s8q4.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the equivalent rate per minute?

medical-s8q5.question: A recorded total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. What is the percentage increase?

medical-s8q6.question: Divide 1.2 L equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each?

medical-s8q7.question: Three sealed boxes hold eight items each. How many items are there?

medical-s9q1.question: A note says “left arm” but the handover says “right arm”. What needs clarification?

medical-s9q2.question: A measurement is written as “12” with no unit. What is missing?

answers.a1: The unit needed to interpret the value

medical-s9q3.question: Which record clearly separates a reported symptom from an observation?

answers.a1: “Nothing happened because the chart is blank”
answers.a2: “Definitely has a diagnosis I have not assessed”

medical-s9q4.question: Why include the time beside a new observation?

answers.a2: To prove the cause by itself
answers.a3: To place it in the sequence of events

medical-s9q5.question: A chart has no entry for a scheduled measurement. What can you conclude?

medical-s9q6.question: Which entry records what happened most clearly?

medical-s9q7.question: Why compare current observations with earlier ones?

answers.a1: To prove a diagnosis from any difference
answers.a3: To avoid looking at the person

medical-s10q1.question: Two people have a headache. Does that alone establish the same cause?

answers.a1: No; symptoms can never help assessment
answers.a2: Yes; each symptom has exactly one cause
answers.a3: Yes; if they use the same word
answers.a4: No; the same symptom can have different causes

medical-s10q2.question: Which is a symptom reported by a person?

answers.a1: A recorded pulse of 90 per minute
answers.a4: A visible wound described by an examiner

medical-s10q4.question: A study finds an association between two variables. What additional claim does that alone not establish?

answers.a2: That one variable causes the other
answers.a3: That an association was observed in the study
answers.a4: That more investigation may be useful

medical-s10q5.question: A person reports an allergy that is absent from the chart. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a1: Clarify and record the information through the care process
answers.a2: Assume the blank chart disproves the report
answers.a4: Ignore it unless another patient agrees

medical-s10q6.question: A patient’s new symptoms conflict with a reassuring earlier note. Which information matters?

answers.a3: Both the earlier context and the new change
answers.a4: Only the spelling in the note

answers.a3: “This finding has several possible causes and needs assessment”
answers.a4: “Questions are unnecessary because a number is available”
